Technical reference

The surfaces an engineer or an agent can rely on: commands, the project folder, settings, how refusals look, and the status output. It points to the page that owns each topic rather than repeating it.

On this page

Commands

Every skill is a /sigma-<name> command. Skills and commands lists all of them with one line each and an anchor per command. Setup flags for hosts other than Claude Code are on Get started: --codex, --cursor and --antigravity, each opt-in.

The .sdlc folder, at a glance

Created by /sigma-init in the root of your repository. The .sdlc folder explains each part.

PathHoldsCommitted?
.sdlc/config.jsonEvery setting.Yes.
.sdlc/project.mdProject context for the agent.Yes.
.sdlc/goals/Goal files, when the backlog is local files.Yes.
.sdlc/features/The unit registry. See Units of work.Yes.
.sdlc/design/Design write-ups from the design step.Plans, research and design records are durable evidence: commit them with the goal that wrote them.
.sdlc/state/, ledger/, work/, knowledge/Machine-written runtime data: the action log, the team ledger, goal worktrees, the knowledge graph.No. Init git-ignores them. Do not ignore .sdlc/ as a whole.

Settings index

All settings live in .sdlc/config.json. Defaults below are what the configuration reference states; Configuration is the full list.

KeyDefaultControls
discovery.sourcegithub when the origin is on GitHub, else localWhere goals come from: issues labelled sdlc:goal, or files.
verify.command, verify.enforceempty, off until a command is confirmedThe test command, and whether a goal can be marked done without fresh evidence.
work.enabledonOne worktree, branch and pull request per goal.
work.auto_mergeoffWhether Sigma merges clean pull requests, and where.
work.require_reviewchangesWhether a requested change or an unresolved thread blocks the merge.
review.independentonAn independent reviewer for the post-pull-request review.
budget.*20 goals, 480 minutes per sessionCeilings on iterations, minutes and tokens for one run.
followups.modein-goalWhether a follow-up joins its goal as a slice or becomes a new goal.
ledger.enabledundecided (off); the GitHub-mode setup question writes itThe committed team ledger.
model_selectionoff in code; the scaffold writes "auto"Per-goal model tier selection. A config without the key stays off; a new /sigma-init writes "auto".
knowledge_graph.enabledoffThe optional knowledge graph.
resource.*derived from the machineMemory and CPU limits for verify and sessions.

Refusals and exit conventions

Sigma refuses loudly rather than proceeding weakly. A guard that blocks something prints the reason and exits nonzero with nothing half-done; a missing guarantee on a platform is a clear "not supported here", not a silent downgrade.

  • Treat any nonzero exit as "stopped, read the message". Specific codes differ by guard (for example, the status renderer refuses with 2 and its output stays empty). Not every guard was checked for a distinct code, so do not branch on one.
  • A goal that needs a person is parked with a reason, not guessed through. See Labels.
  • Some rules are enforced by plain Python on every host, some by a hook on Claude Code only, some only as an instruction to the agent. Trust and limits says which.

The output contract

Status output is never free-form. Every report is one of three blocks, built by a renderer from facts the agent passes it, so the shape cannot drift. If nothing matches a trigger, the agent says nothing.

BlockWhenShape
A, StatusWork is dispatched, slots change, or a turn ends with nothing in flight.Two lines per goal: a marker, the goal reference, a phase token, a title and a model tier; then what is happening now and what unblocks it. At most six goals.
B, EventA phase boundary is crossed, a background task completes, or a merge lands.One paragraph naming the goal, the phase it left and the phase it enters, with one substantive fact, usually that phase's measured cost, and the next action already taken.
C, DecisionA human decision is the only way forward.A blocked marker, the tradeoff in one line, at most three options and a recommendation.

Two axes appear on every status line. The marker says whether the goal is moving: queued, running, in review, merging, done, blocked, parked or waiting. The phase token says where it is: P1 GOAL, P2 RESEARCH, P3 PLAN, P4 PLAN-REVIEW, P5 IMPLEMENT, P6 REVIEW, P7 RETRO.
